sections.h2: What should a Georgia home seller know before listing?
sections.html:
A Georgia sale touches a county tax commissioner, a board of tax assessors, a clerk of superior court and, for troubled properties, the courts. Which office matters depends on the problem, so this page maps the whole state and the guides on this site.

Population gives the scale. The Census Bureau puts the state at 11,302,748 residents in mid 2025, a gain of 5.5 percent over the 2020 base, with 185.6 people per square mile counted in 2020. Its 2020 to 2024 survey figures show $303,300 as the median value of owner-occupied homes and 4,074,366 households, which is the pool of owners the county offices serve.

sections.h2: Which Georgia numbers help a seller judge the local market?
sections.html:
Statewide survey figures give a rough backdrop, and the county gives the detail. Census tables show monthly owner costs of $1,783 for households carrying a mortgage and $541 for those without one, and a median household income of $77,353 in 2024 dollars. Building departments issued 61,196 permits during 2025, so new construction competes with resale homes in many places.

Employers tell a similar story of scale: 261,320 employer establishments and 4,405,730 jobs in 2023. These are averages across 159 very different counties, so a buyer in one corner of the state may face conditions nothing like another. Look up recent sales near your own address at the assessor or clerk's office rather than relying on a state number.

sections.h2: How is Georgia property tax set, and who gets the bill?
sections.html:
Each of the 159 counties runs its own digest. The assessors value every parcel as of January 1, and the state formula takes the assessed amount (40 percent of market value), removes the standard $2,000 state homestead exemption, and applies the millage rate adopted where the house sits. No statewide revaluation calendar exists, so one county may revisit values yearly while another changes little.

The revenue agency says most counties set the due date at December 20, with the bill payable over 60 days from billing. County, school and state tax all arrive on one bill from the tax commissioner. Some counties add homestead relief beyond the state exemption, which is a reason to call the local office before assuming the standard figure applies to your house.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Georgia assessed value?
sections.html:
Disputes start at the county board of tax assessors, in writing, inside 45 days of the mailing date shown on the notice. Mailing the form to the state revenue agency accomplishes nothing because that agency cannot change a local value. The grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and the state publishes the PT-311A form for the purpose.

The form asks the owner to choose one of three paths.

  • Board of Equalization: a hearing is scheduled and the board rules when it ends
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser, offered only for non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000
  • Arbitrator: the owner supplies a certified appraisal, and the side whose number lands farther from the arbitrator's finding pays the fees

Superior court is the last stop. Notice goes to the assessors after the first-level ruling, and the court will not hear the case until tax has been paid at the prior-year level.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
Ownership on January 1 fixes who owes that year's ad valorem tax, and the revenue agency states that a sale on January 2 still leaves the January 1 owner liable for the full year, with no refund for a partial year. A contract can split the bill between buyer and seller, so write the split down and request a payoff figure from the tax commissioner before closing.

A separate excise tax applies at the deed. The Clerks' Cooperative Authority prints it as a dollar for the first thousand of price plus ten cents for every further hundred or part of a hundred, and the seller carries it unless the contract assigns it elsewhere. No deed can be recorded until the clerk certifies payment. The revenue agency says Georgia treats capital gains the same as other income, so ask the Taxpayer Services Division how a home sale gain is reported.

sections.h2: What do Georgia foreclosure and eviction rules mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Lenders in Georgia auction homes without a lawsuit. The borrower gets a certified or overnight letter no later than a month before the sale, and the auction runs on the first Tuesday at the county courthouse. Atlanta Legal Aid lists a pay-off sale ahead of that date as one way out, which makes timing the central issue for an owner in default. Our foreclosure guide goes through each step.

Landlords go through the magistrate courts rather than changing locks. Tenants answer court papers within a week of service, and a seller handing a rented house to a buyer must pass the tenant's deposit along or refund it. The eviction notice and eviction process guides on this site cover those steps one at a time.

sections.h2: Where do the city and county guides fit in?
sections.html:
Think of the guides in three layers. State pages carry rules that hold everywhere, such as the assessment ratio, the appeal window and the foreclosure calendar. County pages cover the offices that bill, value and record, and city pages describe the place a house is actually sold in. Probate, tax sale, estate, landlord and tenant topics sit with the state layer because the law is statewide.

When a local detail is missing, the tax commissioner, the tax assessor and the clerk of superior court are the three offices that can answer it. Bring the parcel number or the street address, and ask for the current bill, the current assessed value and any recorded liens in writing.

faqs.q: What is the assessment ratio for Georgia homes?
faqs.a: Forty percent of fair market value. Tax is figured on that assessed amount after the homestead exemption is subtracted, then multiplied by the local millage rate.

faqs.q: When are Georgia property taxes due?
faqs.a: Normally December 20 in most counties, though some counties set a different date. Owners have 60 days from the date of billing to pay, so check the bill from your county tax commissioner for the exact deadline.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller, by default. A sales contract can shift the cost to the buyer, and the clerk of superior court collects it before the deed goes on record.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Georgia assessment notice?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date on the notice. Send the written appeal to the county assessors rather than the state, and pick one of three paths on the form: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator.

faqs.q: Can a Georgia lender foreclose without suing?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the power of sale in the loan documents, the lender can auction the house outside court once the borrower has had a written notice at least 30 days ahead. A borrower who spots a defect can still ask a judge for relief.
